question.:question/problem: Let $p=⟨1,1,3⟩$ and $q=⟨-1,x,4⟩.$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is zero, find the value of $x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)+1\cdot x+3\cdot 4 \\  & =x+11.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ x+11 & =0 \\ x & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$
